reply:
Only one verse gives a relation, and it is a weak one.

[R 1,42.4] calls Gaṅgā "haimavatī jyeṣṭhā", meaning the eldest, the Himalaya's daughter. The text does not name Himavat directly. The nearby verse [R 1,42.3] has "śailarājasutām", the daughter of the king of mountains, but that is also not a name. Neither verse names a person, so I leave out any daughter_of statement. "Haimavatī" is only a derived epithet, so I do not treat it as a named parent either.

Nothing else in the chapter states a relation. The verses name Bhagīratha as a rājarṣi, but they give no kinship for him.
